tasks.title: Give the control kit its own presentation contracts so it stops naming Application query DTOs
acceptance: Read the frozen contract at C:\Users\dmarq\Development\Repos\dungeon-master\.dir-sdlc\sessions\2026-08-26-settle-the-app-boundaries\contracts\app-core-presentation.cs in full before starting, and section 2 of C:\Users\dmarq\Development\Repos\dungeon-master\.dir-sdlc\sessions\2026-08-26-settle-the-app-boundaries\contracts\new-projects.md. Both are in the MAIN CHECKOUT. Your worktree is C:\Users\dmarq\Development\Repos\dungeon-master\.claude-worktrees\dir\2026-08-26-settle-the-app-boundaries.

AreaItem, FloorItem and PlacedObjectItem exist under C:\Users\dmarq\Development\Repos\dungeon-master\.claude-worktrees\dir\2026-08-26-settle-the-app-boundaries\src\DungeonMaster.App.Core\Presentation\ in namespace DungeonMaster.App.Core.Presentation, with exactly the members the contract declares. Each carries full XML doc comments per dm-conventions/backend/dotnet-format.md section 9: description on its own line indented two tabs from ///, one sentence never broken across two /// lines.

HasNotebookContent is a COMPUTED property on both AreaItem and FloorItem, not a constructor parameter and not a stored field. Both sidebar controls stop recomputing `!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(Description) || !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(Notes)` and read HasNotebookContent instead. dir-architect measured that duplicated expression at AreaSidebarItem.xaml.cs:80-81 and FloorSidebarItem.xaml.cs:153-154 on 2026-08-26. The frontend discipline requires that derived values are computed rather than stored, and that one fact has one owner.

DungeonDetailPresentationMapper exists in namespace DungeonMaster.App.Core.Presentation with the four members the contract declares, AT THE ACCESSIBILITY THE CONTRACT DECLARES. `public static IReadOnlyList<FloorItem> ToItems(IReadOnlyList<FloorDto> floors)` is PUBLIC - it is the one operation an external caller uses. The three overloads `ToItem(AreaDto)`, `ToItem(PlacedObjectDto)` and `ToItem(FloorDto)` are INTERNAL. This is the user's Gate 2 decision on coverage gap 3: an operation with an implementer and no external consumer does not belong on the public surface. The class itself remains `public static class`. It is also the ONLY file in the DungeonMaster.App.Core assembly that names a type from DungeonMaster.Application.Features.*. Prove that: `grep -rln "DungeonMaster.Application.Features" src/DungeonMaster.App.Core --include=*.cs` returns exactly one path, and report that path.

The three internal overloads ARE directly test-covered - criterion 4's error cases are asserted against each overload by name, not only through ToItems - and the visibility that makes that possible is arranged by T1, not by this task. T1 creates C:\Users\dmarq\Development\Repos\dungeon-master\.claude-worktrees\dir\2026-08-26-settle-the-app-boundaries\src\DungeonMaster.App.Core\AssemblyInfo.cs carrying `[assembly: InternalsVisibleTo("DungeonMaster.Tests")]`, following the precedent of src\DungeonMaster.Application\AssemblyInfo.cs and src\DungeonMaster.Domain\AssemblyInfo.cs, which carry the identical attribute today - measured by dir-architect on 2026-08-26 with `grep -rn "InternalsVisibleTo" src --include=*.cs --include=*.csproj --include=*.props | grep -v "/bin/" | grep -v "/obj/"`, returning exactly TWO lines. src\DungeonMaster.App.Core\AssemblyInfo.cs is OUTSIDE this task's ownership set, which is src\DungeonMaster.App.Core\Presentation\** - do NOT create or edit it. Before writing your first test against an internal overload, confirm the file exists and contains that attribute, and report the command you used. If it does not, STOP and report a blocked dependency to the orchestrator: do not add the attribute yourself, and do not widen the overloads back to public to make your tests compile. The evidence this criterion is judged on is your own - tests in src\DungeonMaster.Tests\AppCore\Presentation\ that call ToItem(AreaDto), ToItem(PlacedObjectDto) and ToItem(FloorDto) by name, compiling and passing, which is possible only if the attribute is in place.

No file under src\DungeonMaster.App\ calls any of the three internal ToItem overloads. DungeonMaster.App is a separate assembly with no InternalsVisibleTo grant, so this is compile-enforced rather than a convention, and the criterion-14 builds succeeding is its proof. If any App file turns out to need an individual ToItem, that is a signal the mapping boundary is drawn in the wrong place - STOP and report a contract-change escalation to the orchestrator rather than making the overload public.

The mapper's error cases are implemented exactly as the contract states, and each is covered by a test. A null argument throws ArgumentNullException with the correct ParamName. A null ELEMENT inside floors, floor.Areas or floor.Objects throws ArgumentException naming the collection and the zero-based index, NOT NullReferenceException, and the element is never silently skipped - a floor that quietly loses an area renders a map missing a room, which is the silent-failure class this whole audit is about. No other exception is thrown: an empty Outline, a negative Scale and a whitespace Name all map through unchanged.

The mapper is pure: it reads no ambient state, holds none, is given no cache, and mapping the same input twice yields equal results. Collections are mapped index-for-index so Areas and Objects keep the order the query produced - FloorSidebarItem renders areas in list order and DungeonDetailPage hit-tests them in list order, so a reordering would be user-visible. Cover the ordering guarantee with a test.

AreaSidebarItem.Area is typed AreaItem? and its AreaProperty is created with typeof(AreaItem); FloorSidebarItem.Floor is typed FloorItem? and its FloorProperty is created with typeof(FloorItem); every event on both controls that today carries AreaDto or FloorDto carries AreaItem or FloorItem instead. The BindableProperty type argument and the CLR property type must agree - a mismatch there is the classic control-kit defect, this repository does not have it across any of its nine controls today, and it must not acquire one here.

FloorMapDrawable.Floor is typed FloorItem?, GetEffectiveOutline takes AreaItem, and DrawPlacedObject takes PlacedObjectItem. src\DungeonMaster.App\Graphics\FloorMapDrawable.cs no longer imports DungeonMaster.Application.Features.Dungeons.Queries.GetDungeonDetail.
